title: Two direction changes exclude two exponential modes in 81 of 607 selected Allen curves at a 0.10 error limit
abstract: We tested a constant baseline plus two signed exponential recovery modes in Allen Synaptic Physiology r2.1. The primary sample had 607 selected mouse VisP and human TCx connections, with four pause summaries and at least five trials per pause. The model permits at most one direction change. An exact order test found that 81 curves from 78 recordings need two direction changes after any uniform adjustment of at most 0.10 normalized units. A free constant baseline and any ordered sample times cannot remove these exclusions. At least ten trials left two exclusions among only 37 curves; at error limit 0.20 none remained in that subset. Independent linear programs and synthetic curves checked the test. Passing it does not establish a two-mode fit. The error bound is assumed. Separate protocol trials, uncertain medians, changing states, nonlinear readouts and selected slices prevent a biological mode-count claim. Code, proof, aggregate evidence, source hashes and retrieval steps support reproduction. External records are excluded.

display.caption: Exclusion counts under two necessary order screens. Limits are assumed absolute normalized errors. Curves are selected and are not independent animals.
